rows.what the ink shows: A looped initial d and several tall middle strokes survive, with a dot toward the latter half; dense blue cancellation merges the middle letters and prevents a secure accent/letter-by-letter reading.
The three words show a large looped P, the tall t of tensoriels with a dotted i later in the word, and the h/b ascenders and dotted i of hilbertiens above the underline.

Before the clear capital F of Fredholm, the surviving ink shows a short Op. cluster and a separate small looped de; there is no readable continuous -érateurs sequence. A broad zigzag cancellation crosses both groups.
An initial upright with a top crossbar is followed by the compressed rait strokes and a low connected -ement ending; the middle t stroke remains visible beneath the title underline.

A small two-letter de-like group and a separate nearly horizontal hooked stroke are visible before the large symbol; the latter does not distinguish a complete word or establish the original group boundaries.
The large symbol has two rising arms and a central descender below their cup, supporting capital Psi; the short stacked marks at its right are spatially separate.
The lower interlinear word has a rounded v, a broad low ec group, a tall t, a dot over the later i and a tall final l. Its shape agrees with the clear vectoriel on the body line below.

The initial low a-like loop is followed by a tall l upright and then a separate small g descender; this ascender/descender sequence supports alg- rather than sym-. The compressed dotted middle continues to a long q descender and final ue.
The word begins with the tall looped B, continues through a low an/a sequence and ends in the joined c/h strokes; the dark terminal retracing does not introduce another baseline word.
The small cancelled cluster lies above the baseline immediately right of barred E; intersecting short rays support a superscript star, distinct from the baseline E and its overbar.

An initial d-like loop and a taller b-like loop remain above two strong cancellation strokes, but an independent e is not positively separable. The rest of the phrase and a lower descender/dot cluster remain obscured.
One baseline E has a separate short bar above it, with no superscript letter. After it, the cancellation still leaves the tall t of est and two dotted i positions in ainsi.
The first word has an upright l and a distinct i dot. After the small de group, the descending loop of g and the later p descender remain below the strike through groupe.
The word is one connected low unit ending in a short upright t. The enlarged context has no pair of l ascenders and no second separated word, supporting est alone rather than elle est.

rows.reading: c'est de plus une isométrie (\unsure{au point de vue de} l'identification
rows.what the ink shows: The opening retains c’est, the p descender in plus, and the tall t and dotted i of isométrie. On the next line the final word starts with a dotted i and has later t/i strokes but no paired p descenders, supporting identification; the earlier parenthetical wording remains obscured by cancellation.

A single hooked d and adjacent apostrophe precede the low espace group and its p descender; there is no separate e followed by tall l before espace. The following de and Banach retain the high B and terminal ch.

In the rotated margin, the word after the barred E has an initial p stroke, compressed central turns, and a taller d before the final e. The accent area is faint and crossed by nearby ink, but the sequence supports possède.

The next margin line has an initial s turn, a rising t stroke, and a low connected middle followed by another upright t and the open final e. These strokes are legible enough for structure despite the diagonal neighboring lines.
The end of the margin note has sparse short strokes near the final E and long crossing lines. At enlarged and rotated views they do not separate into a dependable four-word continuation.

There are exactly two baseline E letters, separated by two equality bars; no superscript letter or numeral is visible. Two cancellation strokes intersect the top of the right E, preventing an independent overbar from being distinguished.

After the equality, a curved opening stroke, several low loops and a later upright survive; a further right-hand group has a descending stem and isolated humps. The horizontal cancellations merge these bodies too extensively for a dependable wording.

The first group retains a small hooked e, low s stroke and taller terminal stroke; the last group has a down-and-up u, another rise and a long final exit. The middle group lies on the horizontal cancellation and cannot be separated securely into every letter of encore.

The raised right-hand group physically ends with clear de plus, including the p descender and tall loop of l. Its preceding word has a tall initial and separate short upper mark, and the upper/lower overwritten groups cannot be securely allocated between M0918 and M0919; the whole proposed source span therefore remains uncertain.

The lower overwritten group has an initial loop and upright followed by a long double strike and a surviving loop farther right. The crossings conceal the connecting letters, and the separation from the raised de plus group is not recoverable as two words.

The initial has an upright, detached upper bar and lower curl resembling capital E, while the farther-right low joins could be un. A thick cancellation crosses the middle; neither the complete étant nor a replacement of its exact source span is secure.

The inserted word above the cancelled baseline begins with a short cross-stroke and tall t, continues with a small r/o join, and ends in a dotted i and hooked s. There is no opening looped d or terminal crossing x of deux.
The first short group has the e/s joins and a tall t crossing the deletion line. The second has a looped d, a detached dot and the final t/e strokes still projecting above and below the strike.

After rotation, both tall stem-and-hook bodies have their feet on the same baseline, and each bears a separate raised short oblique prime. The second lateral stroke starts at the very bottom of its stem and is a short foot, not the mid-stem shoulder of h; it is a second L.

At the end of the first cancelled line, a hooked upright, separated horizontal joins and a final doubled downstroke remain. Broad zigzag strokes merge with the low letters and prevent a secure sequence for the words following on.

After the barred E, several low humps and a taller joining stroke survive between the diagonal cancellation bands. Their interleaving with the zigzag and the continuation on the lower baseline leaves no complete word securely identifiable inside this source slot.

The norm formula retains both pairs of vertical bars and the central x near the lower edge. The supposed following words cannot be separated from the broad final cancellation and the higher surviving loops to the right; no reliable two-word reading is visible.

notes: All ten assigned IDs were personally inspected; submitted rows are in source order. Source dimensions were measured with Pillow. No other page image or OCR was used.

Targeted own-ink rechecks resolve M0909 as est and M0911 as d’espace de Banach, and resolve the final word in M0910 as identification. Earlier parenthetical wording in M0910 and cancellation in M0914–M0916 remain uncertain.
Primary elapsed interval includes annotation and coordination time, not continuous active visual reading. Initial report preserved before any targeted revision.

notes.reader: GPT-6 Astra Pro; effort not exposed; run /root/scan044_c
notes: All ten assigned marks were personally inspected without OCR, using Pillow crops, enlargement, contrast and rotation only; all listed scan044 marks were checked for source-span boundaries before the unmarked G was logged.
M0920/M0921 and M0923 were sent to the coordinator for selective independent review; M0918/M0919 also have a concrete upper/lower overwritten-group boundary concern.
M0924–M0926 are heavily cancelled and their original word-count slots do not map securely to separate surviving words; broad source boxes intentionally preserve that limitation.
Hua was consulted only after first own-ink inspection, as an optional competing-source check; it did not determine decisions.

The initial primary report is preserved separately in work/scan044_c.initial.json, with its original finish time. The elapsed primary interval includes analysis and coordination and is not a claim of continuous active reading.

Targeted revision of M0923 is recorded separately; M0921 was not viewed redundantly, and M0918/M0919 retain their mapping uncertainty. The primary elapsed interval includes the wait between initial report and targeted revision.

Following the full lower peer report, M0920 now explicitly retains both étant and $E$ un in whole-span uncertainty; this is an annotation of already inspected ink, not a new visual review. The final own-ink finish remains the M0923 targeted review time.

M0918 whole-span uncertainty was restored by a text-only scope correction: clear physical de plus does not establish its source-token allocation. The immediately preceding report is preserved in work/scan044_c.before_m0918_scope.json.
